MindfulHome needs to be your default home app to work. Tap the button below and select MindfulHome.
Notifications enabled. You\'ll see your timer countdown and gentle nudges.
MindfulHome uses notifications to show your timer countdown and send gentle nudges when time is up. No spam, promise.
Usage access granted. Karma tracking will work.
MindfulHome needs Usage Access to know which app is in the foreground when your timer expires. This is how karma tracking works.
Overlay permission granted. Nudge reminders will appear over any app.

MindfulHome can show a gentle reminder overlay when your session timer expires, even while you\'re inside another app. Without this, reminders will only appear as notifications (which Android may silence over time).
App-switch detection is on. MindfulHome reacts instantly when you leave an app — better for battery.

Optional but recommended. Without this, MindfulHome checks the foreground app on a timer (more battery). Turn it on so MindfulHome is notified the instant you switch apps — faster reactions, less battery. It only reads which app is in front, never your screen content.\n\nTap below, find MindfulHome under Installed/Downloaded apps, and switch it on.

Private, free, offline use is possible with a local model, such as a Gemma3-1B model (557 MB). Download it from HuggingFace and place it in the app's models folder.
Be warned however that small models won't be as smart as you might expect.

For a solution more powerful and less taxing on your space and compute we recommend signing in to use our AI service, powered by Gemini.

If neither is configured, a scripted fallback will be used.

string-array.name: onboarding_philosophy_bullets
string-array.item: Set a timer each time you unlock your phone
Apps earn karma based on whether you stick to your timer
Low-karma apps get hidden (but never blocked)
Talk to the AI to access hidden apps -- it will ask, but always relent
No app is ever closed or force-stopped by MindfulHome

string-array.name: onboarding_app_tiers_bullets
string-array.item: Trusted — apps you know are useful and won\'t waste your time: put them on Quick Launch with no timer
Quick untrusted — useful apps that can still waste time: put them on Quick Launch with a default timer
Untrusted — rarely needed or easy to overuse: leave them off Quick Launch and open them through \"something else?\"

string-array.name: onboarding_layout_bullets
string-array.item: Those rectangles are folders for your Quick Launch apps
A folder with one app launches that app on tap — long-press still opens the folder
You can give apps a default timer, and change it whenever you like
Add, rename, or remove folders as your goals change
Add an app to one or several folders, or remove it when it no longer fits
Change an app\'s timer whenever you need a tighter or looser limit
The \"something else?\" tile opens everything else — your untrusted apps
